before_start: Read this file and run `git log --oneline -20`.
Select exactly one task with status `pending` and the highest available priority whose dependencies are all `done`.
Confirm the selected task's `start_condition` is true before making code changes.
during_work: Work only on the selected task.
Stay inside the task boundary and do not pull in later tasks while working.
Do not modify code unrelated to the current task unless it is strictly required to make the selected task pass its verification.
before_finish: Run every step in `test_steps` for the selected task.
Change `status` to `done` only after all listed test steps succeed.
Write a short execution note in `progress.md` describing what changed, what was tested, and any follow-up risk.
Do not delete tasks or rewrite their scope; only update task `status`.

in_scope: PostgreSQL for business data and server sessions.
Personal workspace auto-created on first login.
One Kanban board per project with default columns.
One Gantt timeline per project backed by the same tasks as the board.
Tasks support title, description, status, priority, start date, and due date.
Task dependencies are included in the Gantt view.

testing: Manual browser verification for frontend tasks unless a task explicitly requires an automated test

tasks.description: Implement `POST /api/auth/register`.
tasks.start_condition: `UserRegistrationService` exists but is not exposed over HTTP, so users cannot create accounts without an admin bootstrap.
acceptance_criteria: A controller in the `auth` module exposes `POST /api/auth/register` as a public endpoint that delegates to `UserRegistrationService` and returns the created user payload (matching the `GET /api/me` shape) with HTTP 201.

The endpoint validates the request body (non-blank login, valid email, non-blank display name, password meeting the configured minimum length) and returns the standard `ApiError` shape with HTTP 400 on invalid input.
Duplicate login attempts return HTTP 409 with the standard `ApiError` shape.

On success the endpoint immediately establishes a Spring-authenticated session for the new user (same mechanism as the login endpoint), so the frontend can hydrate via `GET /api/me` without a separate login call.
test_steps: Add a MockMvc test proving a valid registration returns HTTP 201 with the user payload and an established session (a follow-up `GET /api/me` returns the same user).
Add a MockMvc test proving a duplicate login returns HTTP 409 with the `ApiError` shape.
Add a MockMvc test proving an invalid body (short password, blank login, malformed email) returns HTTP 400 with the `ApiError` shape.

tasks.description: Add frontend register API client and `useRegister` hook.
tasks.start_condition: The register endpoint exists on the backend but the frontend has no typed client or mutation hook for it.
acceptance_criteria: `modules/auth/api/authApi.ts` exposes a typed `register` call that posts the registration payload through the shared `httpClient` (so credentials are included).
`modules/auth/types/auth.ts` defines the `RegisterRequest` type used by the API helper and the form.
`modules/auth/hooks` exposes a `useRegister` mutation hook (TanStack Query) that updates the cached `/api/me` value on success and surfaces backend `ApiError` messages on failure.
test_steps: Run `npm run build` and confirm it succeeds.
Run `npm run lint` and confirm it succeeds.

tasks.description: Build `SignUpPage` and add the `/sign-up` route.
tasks.start_condition: The frontend can register over the API but has no UI to do it.
acceptance_criteria: `SignUpPage.tsx` renders inside `AuthLayout` with inputs for login, email, display name, and password, plus a submit button styled with the existing pastel-green tokens.

The `/sign-up` route is registered alongside `/sign-in` and is reachable when signed out; authenticated users hitting `/sign-up` are redirected to the dashboard, mirroring the existing `/sign-in` guard.
Submitting the form calls `useRegister`; on success the user is navigated to the dashboard (the session is already established server-side); on failure the form displays the backend error message.
Inline validation prevents submitting an obviously invalid form (empty fields, password shorter than the configured minimum).
test_steps: Run the dev server, navigate to `/sign-up`, register a new user, and confirm the app lands on the dashboard with the new account active.
Submit the form with a duplicate login and confirm the form shows the backend error message without crashing.
Submit the form with an empty field and confirm inline validation blocks submission.

tasks.description: Cross-link `SignInPage` and `SignUpPage`.
tasks.start_condition: Both auth pages exist but neither links to the other, so a new visitor cannot discover registration from the sign-in screen.
acceptance_criteria: `SignInPage.tsx` includes a visible secondary link to `/sign-up` for users without an account.
`SignUpPage.tsx` includes a visible secondary link back to `/sign-in` for returning users.
Both links use existing typography and accent tokens (no new colors or sizes).
test_steps: Run the dev server and confirm both links render and navigate to the correct route without a full page reload.

tasks.description: Fix `Sign out` so it ends the SPA session without requiring a manual page reload.
tasks.start_condition: Clicking `Sign out` ends the server session but the SPA keeps the previous user state until the page is reloaded.
acceptance_criteria: Clicking `Sign out` clears the cached `/api/me` value, redirects the user to `/sign-in`, and the app no longer shows authenticated UI without a manual reload.
test_steps: Run the dev server, sign in, click `Sign out`, and confirm the app redirects to the sign-in page immediately without a manual reload.

tasks.description: Fix the server error returned when adding a `depend on` relation to a task.
tasks.start_condition: Calling the dependency-create endpoint from the UI returns a server error instead of creating the dependency.
acceptance_criteria: Adding a dependency through the UI succeeds without a server error and the new dependency appears in the timeline payload and on the Gantt view after reload.
test_steps: From the task drawer or timeline, add a dependency on another task and confirm the request succeeds and the link line is rendered after reload.

tasks.description: Fix the bug where dragging a task to a new column on the Kanban board does not change the persisted task status.
tasks.start_condition: Dragging a card to a different column updates ordering but the task's persisted status stays at the previous value.
acceptance_criteria: After moving a card across columns, the persisted task status reflects the destination column and matches what is shown in the drawer and list views.
test_steps: Move a task across columns, reload, open the task drawer, and confirm the status field matches the destination column.

tasks.description: Align the task drawer's close button so its size and vertical centering match the title input.
tasks.start_condition: The close button on the task edit drawer is visibly smaller than the title input and not vertically aligned with it.
acceptance_criteria: The close button is visually aligned with the title field — same vertical baseline and proportional sizing relative to the title input.
test_steps: Open the task drawer and confirm the close button is centered with the title row at multiple viewport widths.

tasks.description: Replace the default Vite document title `frontend` with `Trackify`.
tasks.start_condition: The browser tab title shows `frontend` instead of `Trackify`.
acceptance_criteria: `index.html` sets `<title>Trackify</title>` and the browser tab shows `Trackify` on every route.
test_steps: Run the dev server, navigate across routes, and confirm the browser tab reads `Trackify` everywhere.

tasks.description: Add a green leaf SVG logo and wire it as the favicon and the in-app logo.
tasks.start_condition: The app uses the default Vite favicon and has no shared logo asset.
acceptance_criteria: An SVG green leaf asset lives under `frontend/public/` (or the equivalent) and is referenced as the favicon in `index.html`.
The same SVG is used as the app logo in `AuthLayout` and in the sidebar header so the brand mark is visible to both signed-out and signed-in users.
test_steps: Run the dev server and confirm a green leaf appears as the browser favicon and as the in-app logo on both auth pages and inside the app shell.

tasks.description: Implement `PATCH /api/projects/{projectId}` for partial project updates.
tasks.start_condition: Project metadata can be created and read but not updated through the API.
acceptance_criteria: `PATCH /api/projects/{projectId}` accepts partial updates for `name` and `description` and persists them.
The endpoint enforces project membership and returns the standard `ApiError` shape for 401, 403, and 404 cases.
test_steps: Add a controller test proving a partial update changes only the provided fields and rejects edits from a user outside the workspace.

tasks.description: Implement `DELETE /api/projects/{projectId}` with cascade for columns, tasks, comments, and dependencies.
tasks.start_condition: Projects cannot be deleted from the API.
acceptance_criteria: `DELETE /api/projects/{projectId}` removes the project and all dependent rows (board columns, tasks, comments, dependencies on either side) in a single transaction.
The endpoint enforces project membership and returns the standard `ApiError` shape for 401, 403, and 404 cases.
test_steps: Add a controller test proving the project and its child rows are deleted while sibling projects in the workspace remain untouched.

tasks.description: Make `ProjectSettingsPage` editable for project name and description.
tasks.start_condition: `ProjectSettingsPage` only displays project metadata in read-only form.
acceptance_criteria: Editing name or description on the settings page calls the project update endpoint and reflects the new values across the app (sidebar, dashboard, breadcrumbs) after save.
test_steps: Edit the project name in the UI, save, reload the page, and confirm the new name is shown in both the settings page and the dashboard project list.

tasks.description: Add project deletion to the settings page with a GitHub-style typed-name confirmation.
tasks.start_condition: Users cannot delete a project from the UI.
acceptance_criteria: `ProjectSettingsPage` exposes a clearly separated destructive `Delete project` action.
Clicking it opens a modal that requires the user to type the exact project name; the confirm button is disabled until the typed value matches.
On success the user is navigated to the dashboard and the project no longer appears in the project list.
test_steps: Open settings for a test project, type the exact project name in the modal, confirm deletion, and verify the project disappears from the dashboard after reload.

tasks.description: Implement `POST /api/projects/{projectId}/columns` to create a new board column.
tasks.start_condition: Board columns are auto-created on project setup and cannot be added later.
acceptance_criteria: `POST /api/projects/{projectId}/columns` creates a column with the given `name`, appended to the end of the project's column order.
Membership is enforced and the endpoint returns standard 401, 403, and 404 errors using the `ApiError` shape.
test_steps: Add a controller test proving the new column is appended to the column order for the project.

tasks.description: Implement `PATCH /api/projects/{projectId}/columns/{columnId}` to rename a board column.
tasks.start_condition: Column names are fixed once auto-created.
acceptance_criteria: `PATCH /api/projects/{projectId}/columns/{columnId}` updates the column name when the user has project membership.
Standard 401, 403, and 404 errors are returned using the `ApiError` shape.
test_steps: Add a controller test proving the column name is updated and that cross-project edits are rejected.

tasks.description: Implement `DELETE /api/projects/{projectId}/columns/{columnId}` and reject deletion of non-empty columns.
tasks.start_condition: Columns cannot be deleted.
acceptance_criteria: `DELETE /api/projects/{projectId}/columns/{columnId}` removes the column when no tasks reference it.
If the column still has tasks, the endpoint returns HTTP 409 with the `ApiError` shape and a message indicating the column must be emptied first.
test_steps: Add controller tests for both the empty-column happy path and the non-empty conflict case.

tasks.description: Implement a reorder endpoint for board columns of a project.
tasks.start_condition: Column order is fixed by creation order.
acceptance_criteria: `PATCH /api/projects/{projectId}/columns/order` accepts the full ordering of existing column ids and persists it atomically.
Bad input (unknown ids, missing ids, duplicates) returns HTTP 400 with the `ApiError` shape.
test_steps: Add a controller test proving the persisted column order matches the request after success and that bad payloads are rejected with 400.

tasks.description: Wire the board UI to manage columns: add, rename, reorder, and delete.
tasks.start_condition: The board renders columns but cannot manage them.
acceptance_criteria: An `Add column` control creates a new column at the end of the board and refreshes the board.
Each column header supports inline rename and a delete action that surfaces a friendly toast when the column is non-empty.
Columns can be reordered by drag-and-drop, persisted via the reorder endpoint, with optimistic state and rollback on failure.
test_steps: Add, rename, reorder, and delete columns in the UI and confirm changes survive a page reload.
Try deleting a non-empty column and confirm a toast explains it must be emptied first.

tasks.description: Implement `DELETE /api/tasks/{taskId}` with cleanup of comments and dependencies.
tasks.start_condition: Tasks cannot be deleted from the API.
acceptance_criteria: `DELETE /api/tasks/{taskId}` removes the task, its comments, and any dependency rows where the task appears as either source or target, in a single transaction.
Standard 401, 403, and 404 responses use the `ApiError` shape.
test_steps: Add a controller test proving deletion removes incoming and outgoing dependencies as well as the task and its comments.

tasks.description: Add a delete-task button at the bottom of the task drawer with a simple confirmation prompt.
tasks.start_condition: The drawer cannot delete a task.
acceptance_criteria: The drawer shows a `Delete task` button at the bottom in a muted destructive accent that fits the existing pastel palette.

Clicking it opens a small `Are you sure you want to delete this task?` confirmation; on confirm the drawer closes, the task is removed from board, list view, and timeline, and the drawer URL state is cleared.
test_steps: Delete a task from the drawer and confirm it disappears from the board, list view, and Gantt view immediately and after reload.

tasks.description: Move task creation into the task drawer with a `Save` action and remove the inline title input on the board.
tasks.start_condition: The board has an inline title input plus an add button to create tasks.
acceptance_criteria: The board no longer renders a title input; only a `Create task` action remains.
Clicking `Create task` opens the drawer (same component as edit) with empty fields and a primary `Save` button instead of `Update`.
Saving a new task adds it to the appropriate column and refreshes the board, with the drawer closing on success.
test_steps: Create a task using the new flow and confirm it appears on the board, list view, and timeline, and persists after reload.

tasks.description: Add a Kanban/List view toggle on the project board page.
tasks.start_condition: The board only supports the Kanban view.
acceptance_criteria: A view toggle (`Kanban` / `List`) is visible on the board page.
List view renders a flat table showing at minimum title, status (column), priority, start date, due date, and creation date.
Clicking a task row in list view opens the same task drawer used by Kanban.
test_steps: Switch between Kanban and List views, click a task row in list view, and confirm the drawer shows the same task data.

tasks.description: Add board filters: title search, status (column) multi-select, and creation date range, applied to both Kanban and List views.
tasks.start_condition: The board has no filtering controls.
acceptance_criteria: A filter bar above the board view supports a title text search, a status (column) multi-select, and a creation date range picker.
Filters apply to both Kanban (hiding non-matching cards while preserving columns) and List view, and are kept in local component state only (not persisted in the URL).
An empty result set shows a clear empty state in each view.
test_steps: Apply each filter individually and in combination, switch between Kanban and List, and confirm only matching tasks are visible.

tasks.description: Implement `POST /api/workspaces` so users can create additional personal workspaces.
tasks.start_condition: Workspaces are only auto-created on first login; users cannot create more.
acceptance_criteria: `POST /api/workspaces` creates a workspace owned by the current user (single owner membership) and returns the new workspace payload.
Validation, 401, and standard error shapes are consistent with the rest of the API.
test_steps: Add a controller test proving a new workspace is created with the current user as owner and listed in `GET /api/workspaces`.

tasks.description: Implement `PATCH /api/workspaces/{id}` to rename a workspace.
tasks.start_condition: Workspace names are fixed at creation.
acceptance_criteria: `PATCH /api/workspaces/{id}` updates the workspace `name` for owners only.
Standard 401, 403, and 404 responses use the `ApiError` shape.
test_steps: Add a controller test proving the rename succeeds for the owner and is rejected for non-members.

tasks.description: Implement `DELETE /api/workspaces/{id}` with cascade for projects and child rows, and refuse deleting the user's last workspace.
tasks.start_condition: Workspaces cannot be deleted.
acceptance_criteria: `DELETE /api/workspaces/{id}` removes the workspace and all projects, columns, tasks, comments, and dependencies inside it in a single transaction.
The endpoint refuses to delete the user's last remaining workspace and returns HTTP 409 with the `ApiError` shape so the user always has at least one workspace.
Standard 401, 403, and 404 responses use the `ApiError` shape.
test_steps: Add controller tests for cascade-delete success, the last-workspace conflict case, and forbidden access for non-owners.

tasks.description: Replace the workspace dropdown with a vertical workspace list rendered in the sidebar.
tasks.start_condition: Workspaces are selected from a dropdown switcher in `AppShell`.
acceptance_criteria: The sidebar renders all of the user's workspaces vertically (similar to the chat list in ChatGPT) instead of a dropdown.
Clicking a workspace selects it and updates the dashboard project list; the active workspace is highlighted with the existing accent token.
test_steps: Run the dev server, switch between workspaces from the sidebar, and confirm the dashboard reloads with the chosen workspace's projects.

tasks.description: Add UI to create, rename, and delete workspaces from the sidebar list.
tasks.start_condition: The sidebar shows workspaces but cannot create, rename, or delete them.
acceptance_criteria: A `+ New workspace` action creates a workspace via the API and selects it.
Each workspace row supports inline rename via a context action.

Each workspace row exposes a delete action that opens a typed-name confirmation modal (same UX as project delete); on confirm the workspace and its projects are removed and the user is moved to another available workspace.
Backend errors (e.g., the last-workspace conflict) are surfaced via toast.
test_steps: Create a workspace, rename it, then delete it via the typed-name modal, and confirm it disappears from the sidebar after reload.
Try to delete the only remaining workspace and confirm the toast explains why it cannot be deleted.

tasks.description: Make the sidebar collapsible with icon-only mode, hover tooltips, and a bottom avatar menu.
tasks.start_condition: The sidebar is always expanded and has no avatar-anchored menu.
acceptance_criteria: The sidebar can be collapsed and expanded via a toggle at the top.
Collapsed state shows only icons (workspace icons + the toggle at the top, user avatar at the bottom); expanded state shows full workspace names and headers.
Hovering any sidebar icon when collapsed shows a tooltip with the full label.
Clicking the avatar (in either state) opens a contextual menu with `Profile` (links to `/profile`) and `Sign out`.
test_steps: Collapse the sidebar, hover a workspace icon to confirm the tooltip, click the avatar to confirm the menu opens, and click `Sign out` to confirm logout.

tasks.description: Extend the `users` table to store an optional avatar (BLOB) and content type.
tasks.start_condition: The `users` table has no avatar storage.
acceptance_criteria: A Flyway migration adds `avatar` (BYTEA) and `avatar_content_type` (TEXT) columns to `users`, both nullable.
The `User` entity exposes the new fields with appropriate JPA mapping (avatar bytes lazily loaded so they do not bloat the default user lookup).
test_steps: Run the backend with the new migration applied and confirm the new columns exist in the local database.
Run `./mvnw compile` inside `backend/` and confirm it succeeds.

tasks.description: Implement profile update endpoint `PATCH /api/me` (display name + avatar) and an avatar-serving endpoint.
tasks.start_condition: Display name and avatar cannot be updated through the API and there is no way to fetch the avatar bytes.
acceptance_criteria: `PATCH /api/me` accepts a multipart payload with optional `displayName` and an optional avatar file; only the fields provided are updated.
Avatar uploads are size-validated (reasonable limit, e.g., 1 MB) and content-type-validated (JPEG, PNG, or WebP); violations return HTTP 400 with the `ApiError` shape.
`GET /api/users/{id}/avatar` returns the stored bytes with the correct content type, or HTTP 404 when no avatar is set.
test_steps: Add controller tests for partial display-name update, avatar upload, avatar retrieval, and rejection of an oversized or wrong-content-type upload.

tasks.description: Implement `POST /api/me/password` to let the user change their password by providing the current one.
tasks.start_condition: There is no endpoint for changing the password from the SPA.
acceptance_criteria: `POST /api/me/password` accepts `{ currentPassword, newPassword }`, verifies the current password, updates the hash, and returns a simple success body.
An incorrect current password returns HTTP 400 with the `ApiError` shape; a new password failing the configured policy also returns HTTP 400.
The session remains valid after a successful change.
test_steps: Add controller tests for successful change, wrong-current-password rejection, and policy-violation rejection (too short).

tasks.description: Build a `/profile` page with editable display name, avatar upload, and password change.
tasks.start_condition: The frontend has no profile page.
acceptance_criteria: A `/profile` route is added and reachable from the sidebar avatar menu.
The page lets the user edit display name, upload a new avatar (with preview), and change password (current + new) using the new endpoints.
Successful avatar upload updates the avatar shown in the sidebar without a manual reload.
test_steps: Edit the display name, upload a new avatar, and change the password from the page; confirm each change persists after reload and the sidebar avatar updates without reload.

tasks.description: Render an avatar fallback showing the first letter of the display name when no avatar is set.
tasks.start_condition: Users without an avatar have no consistent visual placeholder across the app.
acceptance_criteria: Anywhere the user's avatar is rendered (sidebar, profile page, drawer comment authors), a circular placeholder shows the uppercase first letter of `displayName` on a colored disc when no avatar bytes are available.
The disc color comes from the existing pastel palette and is deterministic per user id so the same user always gets the same color.
test_steps: Sign in with a user that has no avatar and confirm the first-letter avatar is shown everywhere the avatar normally appears.
Set an avatar and confirm the fallback is replaced by the uploaded image.

tasks.description: Animate the in-project tab bar's accent indicator so it slides smoothly between Board, Timeline, and Settings tabs.
tasks.start_condition: Switching tabs inside a project simply re-paints the active button with no transition for the accent indicator.
acceptance_criteria: The accent indicator (underline or pill behind the active tab label) animates its position and width when the active tab changes; the page-content swap itself is unchanged.
The animation respects `prefers-reduced-motion` and falls back to an instant change when the user has reduced motion enabled.
test_steps: Switch between Board, Timeline, and Settings tabs and confirm the accent indicator slides between labels.
Enable `prefers-reduced-motion` in the OS or devtools and confirm the indicator change is instant.

tasks.description: Fix task status not updating when moving between columns, and add a status selector to the task edit drawer.
tasks.start_condition: Task status remains unchanged after dragging a card to a different column, and there is no status field in the task drawer.
acceptance_criteria: Moving a card to a different column persists the corresponding status so that reopening the task drawer or reloading shows the updated status.
The task edit drawer includes a status (column) selector; changing it moves the card to the chosen column and refreshes the board.
test_steps: Drag a task to a different column, reload, open the drawer, and confirm the status field matches the destination column.
Change the status from the drawer selector, reload, and confirm the card appears in the correct column.

tasks.description: Fix the Gantt chart being clipped at the viewport width instead of scrolling horizontally.
tasks.start_condition: The Gantt chart area is cut off at the right edge of the screen with no horizontal scroll, hiding bars and date column headers.
acceptance_criteria: The timeline page wraps the Gantt component in a horizontally scrollable container so bars and date headers beyond the viewport are reachable by scrolling right.
The left-side table (Name, From, To) remains visible and does not disappear on horizontal scroll.
test_steps: Open the timeline page and confirm that scrolling right reveals bars and date headers that were previously hidden.
Verify the Name/From/To columns are still accessible after horizontal scrolling.

tasks.description: Fix laggy vertical scrolling on the timeline page.
tasks.start_condition: Scrolling the timeline page vertically stutters noticeably.
acceptance_criteria: Vertical scrolling on the timeline page is smooth without visible jank at a normal display refresh rate.
test_steps: Open the timeline page with 10+ tasks and scroll vertically; confirm scrolling is smooth without lag.

tasks.description: Truncate long task names in the timeline left-side table and inside Gantt bars.
tasks.start_condition: Long task names overflow or wrap unconstrained in both the table column and the bar labels.
acceptance_criteria: Task names in the left-side table are clamped to a single line with a trailing ellipsis when they exceed the column width.
Task names rendered inside Gantt bars are also truncated with an ellipsis and never overflow the bar bounds.
test_steps: Create a task with a title longer than 40 characters and confirm the name in the table column is single-line with '...'.
Confirm the bar label for the same task is truncated with '...' and does not overflow the bar.

tasks.description: Fix the creation date range filter on the Board page not filtering tasks.
tasks.start_condition: Selecting a creation date range in the Board filter bar has no visible effect on displayed tasks.
acceptance_criteria: Setting a creation date range hides tasks whose creation date falls outside the range in both Kanban and List views.
Clearing the date range restores all tasks.
test_steps: Set a narrow date range that excludes some tasks; confirm only matching tasks appear in Kanban view.
Switch to List view and confirm the same filter applies.
Clear the date range and confirm all tasks reappear.

tasks.description: Fix the sidebar highlighting the first workspace instead of the active one when navigating inside a project.
tasks.start_condition: Opening a project board or timeline causes the sidebar to highlight the first workspace regardless of which workspace the project belongs to.
acceptance_criteria: The active workspace highlight in the sidebar always matches the workspace that owns the currently open project.
test_steps: Create two workspaces; open a project from the second workspace and confirm the sidebar highlights the second workspace, not the first.

tasks.description: Fix clicking a workspace in the sidebar not navigating to the dashboard.
tasks.start_condition: Clicking a workspace in the sidebar updates the active selection but does not redirect to the dashboard.
acceptance_criteria: Clicking any workspace in the sidebar selects it and navigates to the dashboard showing that workspace's projects.
test_steps: While inside a project, click a different workspace in the sidebar and confirm the app navigates to the dashboard with that workspace's projects.

tasks.description: Replace the Board status filter buttons with a multiselect combobox (dropdown with checkboxes).
tasks.start_condition: The status filter renders one toggle button per column; with many columns they overflow the filter bar.
acceptance_criteria: The status filter is a single dropdown button labeled 'Status' that opens a list of checkboxes, one per column.
The button label shows the number of selected statuses when any are active.
Toggling checkboxes filters tasks in real time in both Kanban and List views.
The combobox fits in the filter bar regardless of the number of columns.
test_steps: Open the Board filter bar, click the Status dropdown, select two columns, and confirm only matching tasks are visible in both views.
With 6+ columns confirm the filter bar does not overflow horizontally.

tasks.description: Fix avatar upload returning HTTP 500 when the file exceeds the size limit; return HTTP 400 with a user-friendly error instead.
tasks.start_condition: Uploading an avatar larger than the configured limit causes an unhandled server exception and a 500 response.
acceptance_criteria: `PATCH /api/me` returns HTTP 400 with the standard `ApiError` shape and a human-readable message when the avatar file exceeds the size limit.
The frontend displays the backend error message as a toast or inline error instead of a generic failure.
test_steps: Upload an image larger than 1 MB via the profile page and confirm the server returns HTTP 400 (not 500) and the UI shows a friendly error message.

tasks.description: Fix the sidebar overflowing the viewport height so the bottom avatar always stays visible.
tasks.start_condition: With many workspaces the sidebar grows taller than the screen, pushing the avatar below the visible area.
acceptance_criteria: The sidebar is constrained to 100vh at all times.
The workspace list scrolls independently within the sidebar when it is too long to fit.
The bottom avatar / user menu remains fixed at the bottom of the sidebar and is always visible without scrolling the page.
test_steps: Create enough workspaces to overflow the sidebar; confirm the avatar is still visible at the bottom without page-level scrolling.
Confirm the workspace list scrolls within the sidebar independently.

tasks.description: Replace the pure white (#ffffff) background color with #f8f8f6 throughout the app.
tasks.start_condition: The app uses #ffffff as the default background for pages, sidebar, cards, and modals.
acceptance_criteria: All surfaces that currently use #ffffff as background (page, sidebar, cards, drawers, modals) use #f8f8f6 instead.
The change is applied via the existing CSS token/variable so it propagates from a single source of truth.
test_steps: Run the dev server and confirm no pure-white backgrounds remain on the main screens (dashboard, board, timeline, settings, profile, sign-in).
Inspect the root CSS variable and confirm it references #f8f8f6.

tasks.description: Add Day and Week view mode toggle to the timeline page, defaulting to Day view.
tasks.start_condition: The timeline Gantt chart renders in a single fixed granularity with no way to switch view modes.
acceptance_criteria: A segmented toggle with 'Day' and 'Week' options is visible above the Gantt chart.
Day view is selected by default when the page loads.
Switching to Week view changes the column headers to weekly labels and rebins the bars accordingly; switching back to Day restores daily headers.
The selected mode is kept in local component state and does not persist in the URL.
test_steps: Open the timeline page and confirm Day view is active by default with daily column headers.
Switch to Week view and confirm weekly column headers appear and bars reflow.
Switch back to Day view and confirm the layout is restored.

tasks.description: Fix HTTP 500 error when reordering Kanban columns by dragging them between each other.
tasks.start_condition: Dragging a column to a new position triggers a 500 response from the backend column-reorder endpoint.
acceptance_criteria: Dragging any column to a new position persists the new order without any server error.
The columns remain in the dropped order after the drag completes and after a page refresh.
No 4xx or 5xx errors appear in the network tab when columns are reordered.
test_steps: Open the Board page, drag a column to a different position, and confirm no error toast appears and the network request returns 2xx.
Refresh the page and confirm the new column order is preserved.

tasks.description: Fix task not moving to the correct Kanban column after its status is changed in the task edit modal — the move should happen immediately without a page refresh.
tasks.start_condition: Changing a task's status inside the edit modal and saving does not move the task card to the matching column until the page is manually refreshed.
acceptance_criteria: After saving a status change in the task edit modal the task card appears in the column that matches the new status immediately.
The task card is removed from its previous column immediately on save.
No page reload is required to reflect the new column placement.
test_steps: Open a task in the IN PROGRESS column, change its status to DONE in the edit modal, save, and confirm the card moves to the DONE column without a page refresh.
Confirm the card is no longer visible in the IN PROGRESS column after the move.

tasks.description: Fix the Gantt chart calendar header (month, week numbers, or day numbers) not rendering in the top row of the timeline component in both Day and Week view modes.
tasks.start_condition: The date header row at the top of the Gantt chart area is blank — month labels, week numbers, and day numbers are not displayed regardless of the selected view mode.
acceptance_criteria: In Day view the header row shows the month name and individual day numbers aligned with their columns.
In Week view the header row shows the month name and week numbers (W17, W18, …) aligned with their columns.
The header is visible on initial page load and after switching between Day and Week modes.
test_steps: Open the Timeline page in Day view and confirm the top header row shows month and day labels.
Switch to Week view and confirm the header shows month and week-number labels.
Switch back to Day view and confirm the header is still correct.

tasks.description: Add a tooltip that shows the full task title when hovering over a task bar in the Gantt timeline.
tasks.start_condition: Task bars in the Gantt chart show a truncated title inside the bar with no way to see the full title on hover.
acceptance_criteria: Hovering over any task bar in the timeline shows a tooltip with the complete task title.
The tooltip appears within ~300 ms of hover and disappears when the cursor leaves the bar.
The tooltip does not overflow the viewport.
test_steps: Open the Timeline page, hover over a task bar with a long title, and confirm the full title appears in a tooltip.
Confirm the tooltip disappears when moving the cursor off the bar.

tasks.description: Fix the Board/Timeline/Settings navigation tab components rendering larger on the Board page than on the Timeline and Settings pages.
tasks.start_condition: At the same screen resolution the navigation tab pill buttons appear visually larger when the Board route is active compared to the Timeline and Settings routes.
acceptance_criteria: The Board, Timeline, and Settings tab buttons have identical dimensions (height, padding, font size) regardless of which route is currently active.
The fix is applied via shared CSS so all three routes are consistent.
test_steps: Navigate between Board, Timeline, and Settings and confirm the tab buttons appear identical in size on all three pages.
Check at the same browser window size used during the bug report.
